contradictions.detail: The price breakdown lists only a $280 doc fee on top of the $10,233 vehicle price. The dealer boilerplate says prices include the $280 doc fee, a $34 CVR fee and $499 reconditioning. It is unclear whether CVR and reconditioning are embedded or added at signing.

critical_evidence.evidence: The listing is silent on P2440/P2442 history or any SAI pump/valve repair. On a 166k-mile 2010 1UR-FE this is a meaningful open question.
No mention of KDSS leaks, lean or service. Photos show a level stance at rest, but that is not evidence of system health.
The car is in Michigan (salt belt). No frame or underbody photos are examined here and no inspection is reported.
No cluster photo or scan data. The dealer says only 'runs and drives'.

documentation.rationale: The identity/terms half is present: VIN, clean decode, itemised price, and an AutoCheck summary (multiple owners, 0 accidents, clean title) plus a 'Clean CARFAX' claim. The maintenance half is entirely absent: no records, no underbody photos, no SAI/KDSS history, no scan data.

condition.rationale: The dealer states a radiator leak and sells AS-IS. Photos show an apparent rear-quarter dent, hazy headlights and a somewhat tired finish. Frame condition on a Michigan car, KDSS, SAI and fluids are all unproven.

price_value.rationale: $10,513 all-in is roughly 16% below the $12,522 low end of the fair value estimate, after four reductions from $13,000. That discount is partly consumed by the disclosed radiator leak, the as-is terms, the unknown salt-belt frame and an unknown SAI status.

mission_fit.rationale: Body-on-frame 4WD V8 with low range, a full-size cargo area and factory roof rails suits a sleeping platform or rooftop tent. This is capability the RX 350 lacks. The appeal is tempered by high mileage, the cooling fault and the unknown frame condition.

logistics.rationale: Farmington Hills, MI is a fly-out and long drive home from Carmel. PPI access is not stated, though a franchise group with a sister Toyota store nearby makes a local inspection plausible. The radiator must be fixed before a cross-country drive, and CA smog is required on arrival.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Base trim (no Premium/Luxury), first model year, in a less-sought Claret Mica. It is a typical-to-below-typical example with no standout trait.

seller_questions: Will you allow a third-party pre-purchase inspection on a lift (e.g., at your Suburban Toyota store or an independent shop) before any deposit?
Can you send 10+ clear underbody photos: frame rails, rear crossmember, spare-tire area, brake and fuel lines, and the KDSS cylinders?
Can you send a full OBD scan report including pending and history codes, specifically any P2440/P2442 or other air-injection codes?
Where exactly is the radiator leaking (tank seam, core, hose), has the car ever overheated, and will you replace the radiator before sale and at what price?
Can you send a cold-start video from fully cold, showing the dash lights at start-up and the first 60 seconds of idle?
Can you provide the full Carfax and AutoCheck reports, showing owner count, states of registration and service entries?
What caused the dent above the rear taillight on the quarter panel, and has that panel ever been repaired?
What are the tire brand and four DOT date codes?
Is the $10,513 truly the out-the-door figure before tax and registration, or are the $34 CVR and $499 reconditioning added?
Are there any service records, and when were the transmission, transfer case and differential fluids last changed?
Does the vehicle sit level, and are there any KDSS fluid leaks noted during your reconditioning inspection?
Is this car a trade-in from a local owner, and was it driven in Michigan winters?
ppi_focus: Frame rails, rear crossmember, body mounts and brake/fuel lines for salt-belt rust and scaling.
Radiator leak location, coolant hoses, water pump, and pressure test; check for any overheating history.
Valley-plate and timing-cover coolant/oil seepage on the 1UR-FE.
Secondary air injection pump and switching valves; full code scan including history and pending codes.
KDSS cylinders, lines and accumulators for leaks; level check on flat ground.
Transfer case actuator/center diff lock operation and 4LO engagement.
Suspension bushings, shocks and rear air/coil condition; steering rack and front CV boots.
Rear quarter dent: paint-meter scan of the whole body for prior repair.
Tire date codes and matching; brake pad/rotor condition.
Roof rail mounting points and roof integrity for future rack/rooftop-tent use.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: clean underbody photos plus a PPI showing a sound frame, no SAI codes and dry KDSS, with the dealer replacing the radiator or discounting for it.
Up: service records showing regular fluid changes and no prior air-injection failure.
Down: frame scaling/perforation, stored or pending P2440/P2442, KDSS leaks, or any evidence of overheating.
Down: dealer refuses a third-party inspection before money moves.
evidence.mission_note: A body-on-frame V8 4WD GX with factory roof rails supplies the camping and rooftop-tent capability the RX 350 lacks, so it fits the capability branch on paper. As a Base, high-mileage, salt-belt car with a disclosed radiator leak, it is a budget entry point rather than a strong example, and in accelerated_bridge mode it still needs inspection before purchase.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes cleanly to a 2010 GX 460 Base 4.6L V8, and the listing carries an AutoCheck summary of clean title, 0 accidents and multiple owners, plus an itemised $10,513 price. Observed against that: the dealer discloses a radiator that is starting to leak and sells AS-IS, and the photos show an apparent rear-quarter dent and hazy headlights. No maintenance records are offered at 166,073 miles. All four model-critical items are missing: secondary air injection history, KDSS status, frame rust evaluation on a Michigan car, and warning lights. The price sits about 16% below the low end of the $12,522–$15,208 fair value band after four reductions. That discount reflects the known cooling repair and the unknown salt-belt frame. The decisive open questions are frame condition and SAI codes, both answerable with underbody photos and a scan.
evidence.next_action: Ask the dealer for 10+ underbody/frame photos and a full code scan (including P2440/P2442 history), and confirm in writing that a third-party lift inspection is allowed before any deposit.
